newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has alleged that the ruling party is "hatching a conspiracy" to provide transit facility to India and import power from there. The party cautioned it would not tolerate any plot threatening the country's "independence and sovereignty."
A commission will start seeking public opinion from October 2 on the composition, power and functions of a new local government system being planned.

Bangladesh favours a peaceful solution to the Afghan crisis without outside interference, said a foreign ministry spokesman. He said Bangladesh was prepared to play a constructive role within the framework of the efforts of the UN and OIC to resolve the crisis.
Bangladesh tourists are likely to be allowed to visit Nepal by road through India within two or three weeks, said Nepalese Ambassador Lok Bahadur Shrestha.
Bangladesh's outgoing president Abdur Rahman Biswas called upon all political parties to work unitedly rising above party interest for the economic development of the country.
Oman Air on Saturday opened a new route to Bangladesh's capital Dhaka. This is the seventh route of the regional airlines.
Bangladesh has expressed conern and outrage at the violence and killing being perpetrated by Israeli forces in Jerusalem and other parts of the occupied territory.
